newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia will dictate timing of entry into WTO - EU.
newsitem.headline: Russia will dictate timing of entry into WTO - EU.

text.p: Talks this week between Russia and the European Union on Moscow's application to join the World Trade Organisation (WTO) revealed a growing desire to reach a deal, EU officials said on Wednesday.

But while the EU would offer Russia technical assistance in preparing for accession, the timing of its entry into the WTO will be dictated by Russia itself, they told a news conference at the EU Delegation of the European Commission in Moscow.

"Compared to talks we have had in the past, there was a very good atmosphere (at this week's discussions) and the interest in the WTO is rising in various (Russian) ministries," said Ottokar Hahn, Head of the Delegation.
"I can say that the timing will depend on the Russian side, and whether they are willing to move ahead quickly," said Herve Jouanjean, director of WTO trade affairs at the EU.
"We have converging interests in this process moving ahead as quickly as possible," he added.

According to EU trade data, the EU imported Russian goods worth 19.92 billion Ecu in 1995, the last year for which data were available. In the same year Russia imported goods worth 13.52 billion Ecus from the EU.
Some Russian officials have beat an increasingly protectionist drum during the past year because of concern about the health of domestic industries.
But such protectionist rhetoric threatens to dent Russia's relationship with the WTO, which aims for trade liberalisation.
This week's talks were attended by a team of EU experts which had three days of in-depth discussions on Russia's application to join the WTO.
Hahn said that teams from Russia and the EU would next meet in Geneva in April and in Moscow in June.
Russia first applied in 1993, since when four working parties have been held in Geneva.
The Geneva-based WTO was set up in 1995 following the completion of the Uruguay Round of trade negotiations.
